causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace fuse or reset circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 39: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

causes.label: Power surge.
remedies: Unplug the microwave oven; then plug it back in.

causes.label: Plug not fully inserted into wall outlet.
remedies: Make sure the 3-prong plug on the oven is fully inserted into wall outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 39: "Plug not fully inserted into wall outlet."

causes.label: Door is not closed.
remedies: Open and close the door securely.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 39: "Door is not closed."

symptoms.symptom: Floor of the oven is warm, even when the oven has not been used

causes.label: Heat from the cooktop light may make the oven floor get warm.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 39: "Heat from the cooktop light may make the oven floor get warm."

symptoms.symptom: “CONTROL LOCKED” or “LOCKED” appears on the display

causes.label: The control has been locked.
remedies: Press and hold CLEAR/OFF for about 3 seconds to unlock the control.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 39: "The control has been locked."

symptoms.symptom: You hear an unusual, low-tone beep

causes.label: You have tried to start the Reminder without a valid time of day.
remedies: Start over and enter a valid time of day.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 39: "You have tried to start the Reminder without a valid time of day."

symptoms.symptom: Food amount too large for Sensor Reheat

causes.label: Sensor Reheat is for single servings of recommended foods.
remedies: Use Time Cook for large amounts of food.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 39: "Sensor Reheat is for single servings of recommended foods."
